punchline: Andrew Carnegie named his new steel mill after the railroad president he wanted as a customer.
thirty_sec: Dale Carnegie tells how Andrew Carnegie, as a boy in Scotland, got friends to feed his baby rabbits by promising to name the rabbits after them. Years later, wanting to sell rails to the Pennsylvania Railroad, he named his new mill the Edgar Thomson Steel Works, after its president. Jim Farley reportedly knew 50,000 first names. The principle: a person's name is the sweetest sound to them.
question: Whose name could you honor or use more often?
